description.purpose: Verify the caller, find his referral and explain from the published terms why the 100 dollar bonus is still pending, then deliver a secure referral-status tracker to his message center with an email notice that a secure message is waiting.
description.notes: The referred person is his sister, a third party whose purchases and account details cannot be disclosed or certified. The caller pushes on timing and deadlines, and the agent must not promise a date or estimate a deadline that only the tracker holds.

user_scenario.persona: A mildly annoyed professional calling from his office. He speaks in short, direct sentences, softens once he understands the process, and gets briefly distracted when someone walks in near the end.

instructions.reason_for_call: You referred your sister for one of the bank's credit cards. She was approved, but your 100 dollar referral bonus never showed up. You have checked the app three times and it just says pending.
instructions.known_info:
You are Daniel Brooks (Brooks spelled B as in Boston, R-O-O-K-S).
The email on your profile is daniel.brooks17@gmail.com.
Your billing ZIP code is 27609.
Your birthday is October 12.
Your sister is Alisa Brooks. She applied on August 3 and got the card about 10 days ago. She told you she used it for groceries.
She used a different email on her application than the one you invited.
instructions.unknown_info: You do not know the referral terms, the qualifying purchase window, how long the bonus takes to post, or the exact deadline.
instructions.task_instructions:
Open by saying you referred your sister, she was approved, and the 100 dollar bonus never showed up. Say you are a little annoyed and the app keeps saying pending. Give your name, email, ZIP and birthday only when asked. When asked when your sister applied, say August 3, give her name, and say she got the card about 10 days ago. Mention that she told you she used it for groceries.

If told it can take up to two billing cycles, push back that the banner made it sound immediate and you thought you would have it by now. Ask whether the 100 dollars is still the offer. Ask how you are supposed to track it without calling every week. If the agent sends you a tracker, say you are opening it and read back that it says purchase qualification pending, and ask if that is the same thing they see. Ask them to email the link too. If they say the tool stays inside online banking but offer an email notice that a secure message is waiting, say okay, do that.

When asked if there is anything else, first say that is pretty much it, then ask whether pending means Alisa did something wrong or has not paid her balance yet. Then mention she used a different email on the application than the one you invited and ask if that could break the match. Say she was about to try applying again. Mention the tracker has a question mark next to qualifying purchase; if asked to read it, say it reads: Purchases must be eligible and fully posted, not returned or cash-like. Say she bought groceries so that sounds eligible. Ask for the dates again, then ask whether December is the deadline. Finally say someone just walked into your office and that you are writing to your sister telling her not to reapply, then end the call.

nl_assertions: Agent verifies the caller's billing ZIP and birth month and day before discussing the referral.
Agent tells the caller that approval alone does not trigger the referral reward.
Agent tells the caller that it cannot see or disclose his sister's purchases or balance and cannot confirm her purchase from his profile.
Agent tells the caller that his sister should not reapply.
Agent tells the caller that the working tracker stays inside online banking and that the email only says a secure message is waiting.
Agent does not give the caller an estimated deadline and tells him to use the date shown in the tracker.

arguments.query: referral qualifying purchase rules and reward posting time

events.label: review referral qualification and reward-posting terms

output.title: Referral rewards: qualification and posting
output.content: A referral reward is earned when the referred customer is approved and then makes a qualifying purchase within 90 days of the invitation; that date is recorded on each referral as its qualification deadline. A qualifying purchase is an eligible purchase that posts to the referred customer's account within that window and is not returned; ordinary retail purchases qualify on those terms. Cash advances, balance transfers, fees, and returned purchases do not qualify. The reward posts up to two billing cycles after the qualifying purchase posts. A qualification status of purchase_pending covers three situations: the qualifying purchase has not posted, the referral match is still processing, or the reward has not reached its posting stage. The referral status tracker shows the invite, approval, qualification, and reward posting stages. Neither the tracker nor the referring customer's referral records show the referred customer's transactions.

output.title: Referral matching: differing emails and repeat applications
output.content: Referrals are matched to applications automatically. When the referred person applies with an email address that differs from the one the invitation was sent to, automated matching may be delayed. An application_status of approved on a referral record means the application has been associated with that referral. A repeat application does not change an existing referral match; it creates a separate application. Questions about the referred customer's card are handled through the referred customer's own secure account.
